findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from i18next {{n}} to Java MessageFormat syntax, breaking interpolation in the account console
findings.body: The keycloak.v3 account console is a React app whose message bundle is formatted with i18next double-curly-brace interpolation - every other parameterized key in this same file uses '{{0}}'/'{{1}}' (e.g. error-invalid-length-too-short on line 27, error-username-invalid-character on line 14). This change rewrites error-invalid-multivalued-size to single-brace '{0}' plus a Java ChoiceFormat pattern '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}'. i18next does not interpolate single braces and cannot evaluate Java choice syntax, so users who trigger the multivalued-attribute validation error will see the literal string "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." The choice syntax is only valid for the server-side (FreeMarker/Java MessageFormat) bundles under themes/src/main/resources; the React bundles should keep '{{n}}' (and express pluralization differently, e.g. i18next plural forms).

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from {{n}} to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax in the i18next-based admin console bundle
findings.body: The keycloak.v2 admin console messages are rendered by the React admin UI with i18next double-curly-brace interpolation; the previous value of this key used '{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}' like the other parameterized keys in this bundle. The new value uses single-brace '{0}' and the Java-only ChoiceFormat pattern '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}', which i18next cannot interpolate or evaluate. When this validation message is shown in the admin UI, users will see the raw placeholders and the literal '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' text instead of a formatted message. The choice-format variant belongs only in the server-side bundles (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/{login,admin}/messages), not in the React apps' bundles.

findings.title: Missing English reference file aborts the whole verification with a raw RuntimeException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English reference file by string-replacing "resources-community" with "resources" and rewriting the locale suffix of the absolute path with the regex "_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties" -> "_en.properties" (lines 74-75). If the derived file does not exist - a new locale file with no English counterpart, a module whose directory layout does not follow this convention, or an English file named differently - the code throws a bare RuntimeException. verify() only converts IOException to MojoExecutionException, so this exception propagates uncaught and aborts the entire verification run with an unrelated stack trace, instead of being reported as a per-file message like the other problems this verifier detects. The path-based mapping itself is fragile: it silently depends on the exact maven directory naming of every module containing message properties.

findings.title: Diff-highlighting substring can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when common prefix and suffix overlap
findings.body: When a value and its sanitized form differ, the code computes the longest common prefix (start) and suffix (end) and then calls sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) and value.substring(start, value.length() - end). Nothing guarantees start + end <= sanitized.length(). Example: for the value "text><b>y" under POLICY_NO_HTML the sanitizer drops the <b> tag and yields "text>y"; the common prefix is "text>" (start=5) and the common suffix is ">y" (end=2), so start+end=7 exceeds the sanitized length 6 and sanitized.substring(5, 4) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This only happens on the error-reporting path - i.e. exactly when a violation has been found - so instead of emitting the intended "Illegal HTML in key ..." message the build crashes with a stack trace and the actual violation is never reported.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: As part of removing the hardcoded FreeOTP/Google Play links, loginTotpStep1 was rewritten as "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" - which is Italian, not Lithuanian (correct would be e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:"). Lithuanian users setting up an authenticator during login will now see Italian instructions. The same Italian string was also pasted into the Lithuanian account bundle (totpStep1 in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties, line 101).

findings.title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The rewritten totpStep1 for the Lithuanian account bundle is "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" - Italian, not Lithuanian. This appears to be a copy-paste from an Italian translation; Lithuanian users of the account console's OTP setup page will see Italian text instead of Lithuanian.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text used in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle
findings.body: The new totpStep1 value "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" uses Traditional Chinese characters and vocabulary (手機, 應用程式, 安裝) in the Simplified Chinese messages_zh_CN.properties file; the Simplified rendering would be "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：". This looks like it was copied from the zh_TW translation. Users of the Simplified Chinese account console will see Traditional characters, which is inconsistent with the rest of the bundle.

findings.title: No positive test covering valid translations that the sanitizer must accept
findings.body:
All four tests assert that violations are detected; there is no test asserting that a legitimate translation passes verification. The acceptance path contains substantial normalization logic - HTML entity unescaping round-trip, removal of the sanitizer-inserted "" around double-curly-brace placeholders, the "
" (with space) versus "
" distinction, the email RTL style stripping, and the choice-format stripping for error-invalid-multivalued-size / linkExpirationFormatter keys. A regression in any of these (e.g. the sanitizer changing how it emits
or {{...}}) would turn every valid translation into a false 'Illegal HTML' failure and break the build, and the current test suite would give no signal that the verifier ever accepted valid input.
